extra.message: The 'format' value from POST /export/renewals/convert (@Body('format'), import-export.controller.ts:84) is interpolated into a shell command passed to execSync() without any allowlist (unlike convertHealthReport, which restricts CONVERTIBLE_FORMATS and uses spawnSync with shell:false). execSync() runs via the shell, so an authenticated user can inject arbitrary OS commands, e.g. format='pdf; curl attacker'. No @Roles guard protects this route.

saveRenewalSnapshot() joins the user-controlled 'label' (@Body('label'), import-export.controller.ts:74) directly into a filesystem path (path.join(snapshotDir, `${label}.csv`)) with no sanitization. A label such as '../../../some/dir/file' allows arbitrary .csv file writes outside the snapshot directory. The sibling saveEscalationsSnapshot() correctly uses path.basename(), confirming the omission.

importDocumentFromExternalSource() calls fetch(sourceDocumentUrl) where sourceDocumentUrl is taken verbatim from the client-controlled 'x-document-source-url' header (documents.controller.ts:147). There is no scheme/host allowlist or internal-IP check, so any authenticated user can make the server issue requests to arbitrary hosts (http://169.254.169.254/..., internal services). The approved-repository variant validates against a fixed host list, showing this route is meant to be restricted.

continueDocumentWorkflow() passes the client-supplied 'x-workflow-return-url' header straight to res.redirect(workflowReturnUrl || '/documents') with no validation. An attacker can craft a link that redirects a logged-in user (whose browser sends the JWT) to an external phishing site. The equivalent escalations endpoint whitelists allowed return paths (escalations.controller.ts:157), confirming this one is missing the same control.

findStaffByEmail() interpolates the user-supplied 'email' query parameter (directory.controller.ts:12) directly into the LDAP filter `(mail=${email})` with no escaping. The file even defines escapeDirectoryFilterValue() but applies it only in verifyEmployeeBadge(). An attacker can inject LDAP metacharacters (e.g. `*)(|(mail=*))(&(cn=`) to rewrite the filter and retrieve arbitrary directory records. Endpoint has no @Roles restriction either.

searchStaffDirectory() concatenates the user-supplied 'q' query parameter (directory.controller.ts:17) into the LDAP filter `(cn=*${searchTerm}*)` without escaping. LDAP wildcard/metacharacter injection lets an attacker broaden the search or inject additional filter clauses to enumerate the corporate staff directory. escapeDirectoryFilterValue() is only used in verifyEmployeeBadge(), so this path is unguarded.

recordKeyIssuanceForSupportTicket() writes the full plaintext API key (issuedKey: rawKey) plus the entire apiKey object and currentUser into application logs via logger.warn(). API keys are only ever supposed to be returned once in the HTTP response; persisting them in logs (and, combined with the audit interceptor, in the audit_logs table) lets anyone with log/audit access steal live credentials. The rotation path deliberately omits the secret, showing this is an oversight.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log

extra.message: The global AuditLogInterceptor persists up to 500 characters of every non-GET response body into the audit_logs.details column. Responses for /auth/login, /auth/register, /api-keys and /api-keys/:id/rotate contain access_token / plainKey values, so raw JWTs and API keys are written to the database on every such call. This is a persistent sensitive-data leak, aggravated by the plaintext key logging in api-keys.service.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log

extra.message: update() (PATCH /organizations/:id) performs no authorization at all: it never calls assertOrganizationAccess(), takes no ownership/role into account, and the controller route has no @Roles. Any authenticated user - including a customer_contact of another tenant - can overwrite the name, billing contact, renewal date and notes of ANY organization once they know its UUID. Every other mutating organization method checks ownership.

updateStatus() (PATCH /organizations/:id/status) is reachable by any authenticated user (no @Roles on the controller route) and never verifies the caller owns or manages the organization (no assertOrganizationAccess call, unlike updateHealth). A customer contact can flip another tenant's organization to 'suspended' or 'canceled', causing a denial of service, purely by guessing the target org UUID.

issueGoodwillCredit() (POST /escalations/:id/goodwill-credit) updates a goodwill credit keyed only on the path-provided escalation id with no role or organization-ownership check; the controller passes no CurrentUser and has no @Roles. Any authenticated customer_contact can set an arbitrary, uncapped monetary credit on another tenant's escalation. The doc comment claims 'Any internal support rep' but that restriction is never enforced, and draftFollowupReply() also bypasses the DTO, applying an LLM-derived credit with no maximum.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The JWT signing secret falls back to a hardcoded, publicly-known value 'dev-secret-key-change-in-production' when JWT_SECRET is unset, and the identical fallback is repeated in jwt.strategy.ts:19. Any deployment started without the env var can have its tokens forged by anyone who knows this default, leading to full authentication bypass. A strong default-generated secret or a hard failure should be used instead.

exportRenewals() (and exportHealth, exportEscalations, import/contacts and the snapshot/convert handlers) carry no @Roles restriction while import/organizations does, so any authenticated user - including a customer_contact from one tenant - can export every organization's renewal/billing data (billing contact names and emails), internal health notes, and all escalations across all tenants. This is cross-tenant sensitive data disclosure.

For any non-HttpException (e.g. uncaught database/TypeORM errors), the global filter returns the raw exception.message to the client inside the JSON error body (message: [exception.message]). This leaks internal error details, SQL fragments, stack-derived strings and infrastructure information to unauthenticated/authenticated callers (CWE-209 information disclosure).

cwe: CWE-209: Exposure of Sensitive Information Through an Error Message

extra.message: CORS is configured with origin:true (reflect any Origin) together with credentials:true. This makes the API callable from any malicious origin with credentials. Because the app also issues cookies (workspace_context without SameSite hardening in workspace-access.controller.ts), this broad reflection should be replaced with an explicit allowlist of trusted frontend origins.

register() blindly assigns the client-supplied organizationId to the new user, minting a valid JWT with role customer_contact for that organization, without validating that the organization exists, that self-signup is enabled, or that an invite/teamInviteCode was redeemed. An attacker who knows (or guesses) another tenant's org UUID becomes an authenticated member of it and can then read that tenant's customer-visible deals, escalations and documents.
